guidebook.intro: Lusoga has several past tenses. Two will carry you a long way: one for today, one for yesterday and before.

tips.title: Today’s past: -dde, -ze, -ye
body: For something done earlier today, or just now, the verb ending changes: **-lya** (eat) becomes **ndide**, **-kola** becomes **nkoze**, **-soma** becomes **nsomye**, **-mala** (finish) becomes **maze**.
The endings are irregular, so learn each verb as a pair. The same form also says something is done and still true: **Ntuuse** (I have arrived, I’m here).

tips.title: Yesterday and before: na-
body: For yesterday or earlier, put **-a-** after the person prefix: **na-** (I), **wa-** (you), **ya-** (he/she), **twa-** (we), **ba-** (they). The verb stays regular: **nagenda**, **nalya**, **nasoma**.

culture.title: Olide?
body: **Olide?** (have you eaten?) is as much a greeting of care as a question. If you say no, expect to be fed.
